summary.text: Micah King is the Democratic candidate for Georgia House of Representatives District 157 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican Bradley Anderson in a race with no incumbent.
According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he is an accredited financial counselor and a former city councilman in Glennville.

paragraphs.text: Micah King's Ballotpedia survey response describes him as a lifelong member of the District 157 community and the son of Dr. Randy and Sharon King.
It says he works as an Accredited Financial Counselor and as a Transition Career Counselor for the Army Transition Assistance Program, helping veterans and their families plan for life after service.

The response also says he previously served as Ward 1 city councilman in Glennville, sat on the Georgia Municipal Association's District 9 Board of Directors and held the position of First Vice President.

It lists additional roles as youth and young adult minister at Abundant Life Apostolic Church of the Living God, an advocate through the Tattnall NAACP, and a member of the South Tattnall Elementary School and South Tattnall Middle School councils.
King received all 1,803 votes in the Democratic primary for District 157 on May 19, 2026.

In the survey, he named support for family farms, relief from rising costs for working families, and protection of the environment amid real estate, manufacturing and data center development as key campaign messages.
He also said he wants more out-of-school-time and after-school programs in rural Georgia.
